examples.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Multiplication or Division by a Negative Factor
examples.worked_solution:
Note that the factor $2\sin{x}-9$ is always negative. We know this because

$$
-1 \leq \sin x \leq 1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad -11 \leq 2\sin x - 9 \leq -7.
$$

Because $2\sin{x}-9$ is always negative, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity, but we have to remember to flip the sign of the inequality. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9)(2x) & \le 0 \\ \frac{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9)(2x)}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9} & \ge \frac{0}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9} \\ 2x & \ge 0 \\ x & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the factor $3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4$ is always positive. We know this because

$$
0\le {cos}^{2}⁡x\le 1\,⇒\,4\le 3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4\le 7.
$$

Since $3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4$ is always positive, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4)(x-1)}{3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4} & \le \frac{0}{3{cos}^{2}⁡x+4} \\ x-1 & \le 0 \\ x & \le 1.\end{aligned}
$$
